about: Differences a pull request MEANS to make to what the bidding engine sends or decides. Each entry: workflow, check, optional node pattern, field pattern (* matches anything), and a reason in words. An entry excuses differences only in the change that adds it; once on main it is carried over, excuses nothing, and should be deleted. A new entry that matches no difference fails the gate. See README.md, Reading a red.

buyer_select now records how long each live attempt spent before, inside and after the buyer call (#1804), as timing on the attempt row and buyer_call_ms on the node row, so the Stage B latency can be split between the buyer and our own ledger work. Bookkeeping fields on the step rows only: nothing sent, routed or decided changes. The values are 0 here because the replay pins the clock.

buyer_select now times each object call inside a live attempt (#1804): the claim, reserve, breaker record, commit, mark sold, release and buyer_sales mirror, as fields of timing on the attempt row, so the call costing the most can be named from production. Bookkeeping fields on the step rows only: nothing sent, routed or decided changes. The values are 0 here because the replay pins the clock.

The buyer profile copies now carry a switched_off list (the partner id, sale kind and delivery of each disabled profile, #1849 item 3), so a click for a switched-off buyer is refused from the same cache and last-good copy during an outage. The list is empty in these fixtures, and content_hash changes with the new field. Nothing sent to a buyer or decided differs.
